name: MonarchCalendarToolbar
title: CalendarToolbar
wrapsNative: ViewThatFits of HStack and VStack layouts with MonarchButton (Today), Button with buttonStyle(.monarch(.ghost)) arrows, a heading Text, ProgressView with .monarchCircular, and Menu holding Picker with pickerStyle(.inline) for the view
summary: The header of a calendar: Today, previous and next, the range title with a busy indicator, a menu that switches between day, week, month and agenda views, and the app's actions.
whenToUse: Above a calendar view (a month grid, a week, an agenda) whose range the person moves through.
whenNotToUse: For choosing one date use DatePicker (see date-picker). For a screen title use the navigation bar; for two to four view choices with no navigation use Picker with pickerStyle(.segmented).
api: MonarchCalendarToolbar.init(_ title: String, view: Binding<MonarchCalendarToolbarView>, views: [MonarchCalendarToolbarView] = MonarchCalendarToolbarView.allCases, isBusy: Bool = false, isTodayDisabled: Bool = false, isPreviousDisabled: Bool = false, isNextDisabled: Bool = false, labels: MonarchCalendarToolbarLabels = MonarchCalendarToolbarLabels(), onToday: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void, onPrevious: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void, onNext: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void, @ViewBuilder actions: () -> Actions)

options.name: title
options.description: The range shown, already formatted: "November 2026", "2 – 8 Nov 2026". Announced when it changes.

options.name: view
options.description: The current view. The switcher sets it, and the arrows are named for its unit.

options.name: views
options.description: The views offered, in order. With one view or none the switcher is not shown.

options.name: isBusy
options.description: Shows a small circular progress indicator, named "Loading", after the title.

options.name: isTodayDisabled
options.description: Disables Today, for example when the range already contains today.

options.name: isPreviousDisabled
options.description: Disables the previous arrow, for example at the start of a booking window.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Today", "Previous week", "Next week", "Calendar view", the view names, the units and "Loading".

options.name: onToday
options.description: Moves to the range that contains today.

options.name: onPrevious
options.description: Moves back one unit of the view.

options.name: onNext
options.description: Moves forward one unit of the view.

options.name: actions
options.description: Controls at the end: a New event button, a filter menu, a DatePicker. Pass it labelled, actions: { … }.

states.name: one line
states.description: Today, the arrows, the title, then the switcher and actions at the end.

states.name: two lines
states.description: When one line does not fit, the title goes on its own line above the controls.

states.name: stacked
states.description: At the largest text sizes the title, the navigation and the switcher with actions are on three lines.

states.name: busy
states.description: A small circular progress indicator after the title.

states.name: disabled controls
states.description: Today and either arrow can be disabled; they take the button style's disabled colours.

appearance: The title uses the heading type role in the default text colour. Today and the switcher are secondary Monarch buttons, the arrows ghost buttons, all at the sm size; the busy indicator uses the accent. Every colour comes from the theme, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The parity map named .toolbar items. A navigation bar has no room for Today, two arrows, a title, a switcher and actions at large text sizes, and toolbar placements differ between iPhone and iPad, so this is a header view that reflows with ViewThatFits; place it above the calendar or in safeAreaInset(edge: .top). The web's titleAs (heading level) is the header trait; its datePicker slot is part of actions. The web accepts product-defined view ids; this enum has the four built-in views only. Android builds the same component with the same name.
accessibility: The title has the header trait and is announced with AccessibilityNotification.Announcement when it changes.
The arrows are named for the view's unit ("Previous week", "Next month"); their chevrons are backward and forward symbols, so they follow the reading direction.
The switcher is a Menu named "Calendar view" whose value is the current view; inside it the system Picker marks the selected view.
Every button has a touch target of at least 44 by 44 points; the layout reflows instead of truncating at large text sizes.
edgeCases: A long title wraps on its own line instead of pushing the controls off screen.
With views set to one view the switcher is hidden, but that view still names the arrows.
The announcement fires on every title change, including the app's own; set the title once per move.
